subject: Pricing: per-1M IO rates + model options (Marketly POC)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@marketly.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@marketly.io
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Quick pricing question: per-1M token IO rates + supported models

Hi Karthik,

We're getting ready to scope a short POC (Marketly Inc.) and need a baseline for hosted API economics. Two quick asks: 1) your standard per-1M token IO split (input vs output) for hosted endpoints, and 2) a short list of recommended models (small / medium / large) that you typically surface for latency-sensitive web apps.

For the POC we expect ~5M tokens/month (mostly generation, some embeddings) and then 10-20M/mo if we go to production. Also curious about any starter volume discounts or commit structures you offer.

Can you send the standard rate sheet and a one-page estimate for 5M vs 20M tokens? Procurement is looped for contracting questions.

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Products, Marketly
samir@marketly.io
+1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the note and context. Happy to put together a short-rate snapshot and a simple workbook modeling 5M vs 20M tokens. A couple quick clarifying Qs so I give you the right mixes:
- Is the 5M estimate mostly output-heavy (e.g., assistant-style responses) or balanced input/output?
- Do you need streaming responses for the POC low-latency UI, or are batch responses acceptable?
- Any compliance constraints beyond standard SOC2 (e.g., data residency)?

I'll attach our current public ratecard (pdf) and an editable estimate workbook. Marissa (pricing) and Jonas (solutions) are on cc — I’ll propose a baseline and one commit path so procurement can review. Expect an updated email with numbers by EOD Monday PST.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer

karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir@marketly.io>

Subject: Re: Quick pricing question: per-1M token IO rates + supported models

Karthik —

Thanks. Quick answers:
- POC will be output-heavy (~70% output). Most prompts are short (few hundred tokens) but responses average ~450 tokens.
- We prefer streaming for UX but can fall back to chunked responses if needed.
- SOC2 is sufficient for our initial review; we may need EU data residency later but not for POC.

We’re targeting a fast start: sign SOW within two weeks if the economics look reasonable. Procurement copy here (procurement@marketly.io) — they’ll want the formal rate table and any standard MSA/ordering attachments.

Samir

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jan 2029 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Marketly pricing ask — proposed approach (internal)

Team — forwarding Marketly thread. They’re POCing at ~5M tokens/mo and expect to scale to 10-20M. They prefer streaming and output-heavy usage. Procurement is waiting.

My suggested commercial paths:
- Option A (no commit): Published hosted rates (IO split) — low friction for POC.
- Option B (3-mo pilot commit): 10% off hosted IO rates for first 3 months with a 50% uplift credit applied to overage if they hit >12M in any month.
- Option C (12-mo consumption commit): 18% discount on IO rates + waived onboarding fee for 12-month committed baseline (predictable throughput; we offer reserved capacity onboarding).

Propose we surface Option A + B in the first outbound to keep things moving; leave the deep commit (C) as a later negotiation once they validate performance.

Pricing specifics to propose in outbound (examples):
- small models (low-latency): input $0.15 /1k, output $0.45 /1k
- medium models (best cost/quality): input $0.10 /1k, output $0.35 /1k
- large models (highest quality): input $0.06 /1k, output $0.60 /1k

Those are back-of-envelope — Marissa, can you confirm current published rates and whether we can front-load a 10% pilot discount without legal changes? Jonas, can you confirm that streaming (client tokens) won't materially change expected unit cost for the POC.

Karthik

--

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Marketly POC — baseline rates + pilot discount (proposal)

Hi Samir / procurement team —

Appreciate the details. Per our thread, attached is a concise snapshot and an editable workbook modeling 5M and 20M tokens/month. Summary below (hosted API, per-1M tokens):

Baseline published IO rates (per 1M tokens):
- Small / low-latency models: input $150.00, output $450.00
- Medium / balanced models: input $100.00, output $350.00
- Large / high-quality models: input $60.00, output $600.00

Pilot discount (Option B) — 3-month pilot commit: 10% off the above IO rates for the first 3 months. If any single month exceeds 12M tokens, we apply a 50% uplift credit on overage to accelerate into a standard committed discount discussion.

Model guidance for the POC (recommended shortlist):
- Small: redwood-lite-4b (fastest, <50ms p50 per-token on hosted tier)
- Medium: redwood-standard-13b (balanced latency/quality)
- Large: redwood-xxl-65b (highest quality; recommend only when generation quality trumps latency)

Attachments included: redwood-standard-ratecard-v3.pdf, marketly-poc-estimate.xlsx (workbook with line-item estimates for 5M and 20M tokens).

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, procurement can confirm via email and we’ll issue a standard SOW + one-page pilot attachment reflecting Option B.
2) If you want firm committed pricing (Option C), Marissa can draft a consumption commit sheet — we’ll need a target monthly baseline.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the workbook. Available tomorrow 10–11am PT if that works for you.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
